title: A Bell for the Visitor
premise: When Felix Reyes returns to the decaying town of Vesper's Hollow to bury his twin sister Marisol, he insists on a rational explanation for the strange bell that rings at dusk from the hillside excavation site. But the crew has unearthed an iron door sealed from the inside, and the town's founding families have been keeping a bargain: every generation invites one visitor in, and the thing below leaves everyone else alone. Marisol was the invited one, and her death has broken the contract. Over one long night, Felix, the crew forewoman Odette, and Marisol's grieving partner Camille must decide whether to renew the invitation, expose the truth, or hold the door until sunrise—discovering that Marisol's death was not an end but an opening, and that Felix himself was the visitor the town invited all along. In the end, Felix chooses truth over the town's survival, ringing the bell himself to call the thing back down, and walks out at dawn carrying a grief that is finally, terribly his own.
about_author: Xanthe Marchetti is the pen name of a former mortuary transcriptionist who spent six years cataloguing small-town funeral records across the Rust Belt. Their fiction explores what communities bury to keep functioning, and what insists on being exhumed.

chapters.title: The Wrong Sibling
chapters.summary: Felix arrives in Vesper's Hollow for Marisol's funeral, numb and skeptical of the town's hushed condolences. POV Felix. Beat: grief sharpened into denial as he notices the townspeople watching him like he's someone else.

chapters.title: Bell at Dusk
chapters.summary: At the wake, a distant bell tolls from the ridge where the highway excavation is underway; every local stops mid-motion, then resumes as if nothing happened. POV Camille, Marisol's partner. Beat: dread of knowing what the sound means and being unable to say it aloud.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: Forewoman Odette shows Felix the excavation: an iron door set into bedrock, bolted and barred from within, older than the town charter. POV Odette. Beat: professional pride curdling into fear as she admits the crew found handprints on the inside.

chapters.title: What the Founders Kept
chapters.summary: Felix searches Marisol's house and finds her research: founding-family ledgers listing one 'Visitor' per generation, each entry crossed out on the date of a disappearance. POV Felix. Beat: his rationalism cracks as the pattern refuses coincidence.

chapters.title: The Invitation Rite
chapters.summary: Camille confesses the town's bargain: the elders invite one willing soul to the door each generation, and the thing below honors the rest. Marisol volunteered. POV Camille. Beat: guilt and love colliding—she helped Marisol prepare and never stopped her.

chapters.title: Marisol's Last Letter
chapters.summary: Felix finds a letter addressed to him, written the night before Marisol walked up the ridge, asking him to believe just once, for her. POV Felix. Beat: fury at her secrecy dissolving into the first vertigo of belief.

chapters.title: The Door Is Open
chapters.summary: At dawn the excavation crew reports the door standing ajar, the bars bent outward. Odette seals the site, but one worker, Reyes's old classmate Denny, is missing. POV Odette. Beat: the moment containment becomes impossible.

chapters.title: Elders in the Dark
chapters.summary: The founding families convene in the church basement; Felix and Camille force their way in and hear them debate renewing the invitation with a new name. POV Felix. Beat: horror at learning his sister's death was procedure, not tragedy.

chapters.title: They Want a Name
chapters.summary: The elders propose writing Felix's name into the ledger—twins share the invitation, they claim, and the contract can be amended. POV Camille. Beat: protective love against the town's cold arithmetic.

chapters.title: Denny Comes Home
chapters.summary: Denny returns at dusk, unharmed and serene, speaking of the visitor below in Marisol's cadence. The bell rings twice. POV Odette. Beat: the uncanny made intimate; the crew realizes Denny is a mouthpiece now.

chapters.title: Rules of the Night
chapters.summary: Camille lays out the old rules: keep the bell ringing, keep the door in sight, don't answer to your name after midnight, hold out until sunrise. POV Camille. Beat: found-family resolve as the three outsiders bind together against the town.

chapters.title: First Watch
chapters.summary: The trio fortifies the excavation office; the power fails and the bell falls silent, and something begins testing the doors with Marisol's voice. POV Felix. Beat: his disbelief becomes a weapon—he refuses to answer, and it holds.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Last Page
chapters.summary: Felix reads the ledger to the final page and finds his own name already entered, in his mother's handwriting, dated the night of his birth. POV Felix. Beat: the premise's turn—he was the invited visitor; Marisol died in his place.

chapters.title: What Mother Did
chapters.summary: A dying elder explains: their mother substituted Marisol's name for Felix's thirty years ago, an act of love that the thing below has finally come to correct. POV Odette. Beat: duty and maternal love revealed as the original sin of the story.

chapters.title: The Town Decides
chapters.summary: The townspeople, terrified of reprisal, come to the site to drag Felix to the door themselves; Odette and Camille hold the barricade. POV Odette. Beat: loyalty vs. truth—the town chooses its survival over one man's life.

chapters.title: Camille at the Door
chapters.summary: Camille offers herself in Felix's place, claiming Marisol's invitation can pass to her partner; the bell tolls once, considering. POV Camille. Beat: love against duty made literal—she would rather be taken than let Felix go.

chapters.title: Marisol's Voice
chapters.summary: The thing speaks to Felix in Marisol's true voice, not the imitation, and tells him the truth: it doesn't want a body, it wants a willing bell-ringer to let it out. POV Felix. Beat: temptation—the chance to hear his sister again forever.

chapters.title: The Bargain Refused
chapters.summary: Felix refuses to open the door and refuses to give it anyone; the elders, enraged, move to ring the bell themselves and force the contract. POV Felix. Beat: his choice crystallizes—truth over the town's lie, whatever it costs.

chapters.title: Riot at the Ridge
chapters.summary: The elders and the trio struggle at the door as the thing below pushes; Denny, half-himself, turns on his masters and bars the door from the outside. POV Odette. Beat: the betrayer's redemption; the crew's loyalty holds under maximum pressure.

chapters.title: Felix Rings
chapters.summary: Understanding that the bell calls the visitor home, Felix climbs the scaffold and rings it himself, naming himself the visitor and then un-inviting himself—renouncing the contract in the ledger with his own blood. POV Felix. Beat: climax—love for Marisol transformed into truth-telling; the door groans shut from the inside once more.

chapters.title: Sunrise
chapters.summary: The thing withdraws; the elders' power breaks as the crew broadcasts the ledger's truth to the town; Denny does not wake, and Camille buries him beside Marisol. POV Camille. Beat: grief shared openly at last—found family over found tradition.

chapters.title: A Bell for the Visitor
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Felix stays in Vesper's Hollow to help dismantle the excavation and seal the ridge with concrete; the bell hangs silent in the town square as a warning, not a summons. POV Felix. Beat: resolution—he finally believes, and belief means staying; he visits Marisol's grave and tells her the truth at last.
